title: Rohit Sharma's Lord's Century Reshuffles ICC ODI Rankings Battle
excerpt: The veteran opener's record-breaking 138 at Lord's narrows the gap with Virat Kohli in the ICC batting rankings, while Shubman Gill continues to chase New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell for the No. 1 spot.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rohit Sharma's 138 at Lord's boosts his ICC ODI ranking, closing in on Virat Kohli.
  • Shubman Gill scored 188 runs in the series, just 11 points behind No. 1 Daryl Mitchell.
  • India lost the ODI series 1-2 to England but retained the No. 1 team ranking with 116 points.
  • The rankings are crucial as the 2027 ODI World Cup approaches in less than a year.
  • Rohit Sharma's 138 at Lord's — the first ODI century by an Indian at the venue — is set to significantly boost his ICC ODI batting rankings from 744 points, narrowing the gap with Virat Kohli (757 points pre-series).
  • Shubman Gill, with 188 runs across the series at an average of 62.66, has closed to within 11 rating points of No. 1-ranked Daryl Mitchell.
  • India lost the three-match ODI series 1-2 to England but retained the No. 1 team ranking with 116 points despite dropping five points.
  • The rankings race gains significance with the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia less than a year away.

The ICC ODI batting rankings are witnessing a multi-front battle involving three Indian batters, with Rohit Sharma's commanding century at Lord's threatening to redraw the standings heading into the 2027 World Cup cycle.

Entering the recently concluded England series, New Zealand's Daryl Mitchell held the No. 1 spot with 814 rating points, followed by India captain Shubman Gill at 803, Virat Kohli at 757, and Rohit at 744, according to CricTracker. After three matches against England and a parallel NZ-West Indies series, those margins have been compressed dramatically.

Rohit's Lord's Masterclass

Rohit began the England tour quietly, managing just 11 and 26 in the first two ODIs at Edgbaston and Cardiff. Then came July 19 at Lord's.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=BzfN3Oo0QHY

Chasing 388, the 39-year-old opener hammered 138 off 110 balls in what Cricbuzz confirmed was the first ODI century by an Indian batter at the Home of Cricket. At 39 years and 80 days, he also became the oldest player to score an ODI hundred at the venue, surpassing Rahul Dravid's previous age record for India across all formats at Lord's.

"Rohit and Kohli, this will always be a problem for them because an ODI series is generally of three matches. There is a series, then there is nothing for two months."

— Aakash Chopra, former India opener

"England remain seventh at 93 points."You want to score runs."

The knock was Rohit's eighth ODI century in England — more than any visiting batter in a single country, according to Cricbuzz. It was also his 18th hundred in ODI run chases, second only to Kohli's 29. He finished the series with 175 runs at an average of 58.33, making him India's standout performer alongside Gill.

Gill's Pursuit of the No. 1 Spot

While Rohit generated the headlines, India's ODI captain Gill quietly posted the highest aggregate of any Indian batter in the series: 188 runs at 62.66, including an unbeaten 80 in the Edgbaston win and 77 at Lord's.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DaKVxFPqK9V/

After the first ODI, the ICC confirmed that Gill had gained 12 rating points, leaving him just 11 behind Mitchell. The New Zealander, meanwhile, accumulated 93 runs across the first two matches of a parallel five-match series against the West Indies, maintaining his lead at the summit.

With both series now concluded — New Zealand sealed a 3-1 win over the West Indies — the final rankings update will determine whether Gill has done enough to overtake Mitchell. A single strong knock or series-ending slump can shift the balance by 20 or more rating points in bilateral contests.

Kohli Finds Form Late

Kohli entered the series at No. 3 with 757 points. After a quiet start in Birmingham, he scored 65 at Sophia Gardens and 74 at Lord's, finishing with 144 runs at an average of 48 and a strike rate above 100. The two half-centuries should consolidate his position, but Rohit's superior output — particularly the Lord's century — is expected to bring the gap between the two former captains to single digits.

The pair also reached a milestone at Lord's, appearing together in their 400th international match as teammates, according to SportsTak. They are the first Indian duo to achieve the feat, having accumulated a combined 48,574 runs and 135 centuries across formats. Their 21 century partnerships in ODIs trail only Sachin Tendulkar and Sourav Ganguly's 26.

What the Rankings Mean for 2027

The jockeying for position carries real significance. The 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe, and Namibia is less than a year away, and individual rankings influence seedings, public perception, and squad selection debates.

India retained the No. 1 team ranking with 116 points despite losing the series to England 1-2, according to Wisden, though the five-point drop has allowed New Zealand (111 points) to narrow the gap. England remain seventh at 93 points.

"You want to score runs. They generally don't fail in the same match... this could be their last England tour."

— Aakash Chopra, on Rohit and Kohli's urgency

For Rohit, 39, and Kohli, 37 — both now playing only ODIs at the international level — the scheduling challenge is acute. ODI series are typically three matches long with months-long gaps between them. India's next ODI assignment is not until September, creating an extended break that Chopra flagged as a structural disadvantage for veteran batters trying to maintain rhythm.

The full post-series ICC rankings update will confirm the exact movement across all positions. For Indian fans, the key question is whether Gill can finally dislodge Mitchell from the top spot and whether Rohit's Lord's heroics have pulled him level with — or past — Kohli in the standings. With England's Ben Duckett (141 at Lord's) and Joe Root (249 unbeaten runs in the series) also likely to climb, the upper reaches of the ODI rankings table are set for their most competitive phase in years.
